claim: For the original unsaturated age-structured predator-prey role-reversal model of Suarez, Cameron, Fagan and Levy, let \(x(t)>0\) be prey abundance, \(u(t,\tau)\ge0\) the predator age density, \(y(t)=\int_0^\infty u(t,\tau)\,d\tau\), and let \(y_1\) and \(y_2\) be the juvenile and adult masses split at the maturation age \(\tau^*\). If \(g>k\) and \(2sk\le b(g-k)\), then the source's local positive solution extends to every finite time; in particular, mathematical finite-time blow-up is impossible in this parameter region. With the convention \(b/k=+\infty\) when \(k=0\), every \(c\in[2s/(g-k),b/k]\) gives \(V=x+cy\) satisfying \(V'(t)\le C V(t)\), where \(C=\max\{r,\|\widetilde B\|_\infty\}\), and hence \(V(t)\le V(0)e^{Ct}\). The condition is exact for existence of a constant weight \(c>0\) that makes every prey-predator cross-interaction term nonpositive for all ages under the paper's smooth logistic maturation functions. This does not assert uniform-in-time boundedness, exclude growth past the paper's numerical threshold of 1000, or rule out divergence as \(t\to\infty\).
integrity: The source model equations, smooth maturation functions, local existence theorem, numerical blow-up rule, and saturated-model discussion were read in the open-access full text.
The earliest verified public date is arXiv v1 on 2025-02-27, not the later journal date.
The proof is analytic; exact-rational code only checks algebraic bookkeeping.
scientific_limitations: The theorem excludes finite-time norm blow-up but does not prove a uniform-in-time population bound or exclude divergence as time tends to infinity.
The source uses an operational numerical blow-up threshold of 1000; the theorem does not prevent such a threshold crossing.
The parameter condition is sharp only for constant weighted masses of the form \(V=x+c\int u\).
title: A weighted-mass criterion rules out finite-time blow-up in the unsaturated age-structured role-reversal model
